text.p: The Australian government's blitz on its budget deficit has upset the country's usually placid public servants, who protested against staff cuts with a 13-minute "Black Friday" strike.
The striking public servants were protesting against both their falling numbers and the conservative government's decision to water down their employment conditions.
The strike, organised by the main public sector trade union representing 60,000 public servants, was billed as a symbolic "Black Friday" stoppage for Friday the 13th.

"It was a bit of unusual action in addition to our usual industrial strategies and people enjoyed doing it and thought it was a good piece of industrial action," Commonwealth and Public Sector Union national secretary Wendy Caird told Reuters.
Australia's Liberal-National government has cut staffing in the two budgets it has announced since it won office in March 1996.
The country's capital Canberra, disliked by the rest of the country as a cosseted haven for public servants, is also suffering as the cuts send its traditionally stable economy into recession.
Canberra has suddenly found itself a company town with the company laying off staff.
It has no other major industry. Much of its private sector is a support service for the bureaucracy, and the government is cutting back spending on contractors, too.
